A monarch ( / ˈ m ɔː n ɑː r k / ) is a head of state [ 1 ] [ 2 ] for life or until abdication , and therefore the head of state of a monarchy . A monarch usually exercises the highest authority and power in the state . [ 3 ] Usually, a monarch either personally inherits the lawful right to exercise the state's sovereign rights (often referred to as the throne or the crown ) or is selected by an established process from a family or cohort eligible to provide the nation's monarch. [ 4 ] Alternatively, an individual may proclaim oneself monarch, or even usurp power, as many Ancient Greek tyrants did. [ 5 ] If a young child is crowned the monarch, then a regent is often appointed to govern until the monarch reaches the requisite adult age to rule. [ 6 ]
